title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from SpaceX's latest launch to new partnerships in satellite technology. Meanwhile, budget allocations are shifting, and hypersonic tests continue to stumble.

themes.title: SpaceX's Rideshare Dilemma
themes.body: SpaceX's Transporter-17 launch raises eyebrows about the viability of its rideshare program amid increasing competition. With the Pentagon backing a new satellite, the stakes are higher than ever.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience initiatives, signaling a growing commitment to safeguarding assets in orbit. This influx of cash could reshape priorities in an already crowded market.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: Yet again, hypersonic glide-vehicle tests have slipped, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This ongoing struggle raises questions about the pace of innovation in a field where speed is paramount.

themes.title: New Players in Satellite Game
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, reflecting a trend of established defense firms seeking to capitalize on emerging satellite technologies. Meanwhile, Simera Sense's involvement in the Canary Islands constellation highlights the growing interest in Earth observation.
